paragraphs.text: Esther maketh a petition for her own and her people’s life, Est 7:1-4. She accuseth Haman, who had determined to destroy the Jews, Est 7:5,6. Haman is afraid, Est 7:6. The king in his anger, Est 7:7,8, being informed of the gallows which Haman had built for Mordecai, causeth him to be hanged thereon, Est 7:9,10.
so it is called, to note that it was not designed for a feast to fill their bellies, but rather for a banquet to delight and please their palates with wine and other delicacies: See Poole "Est 5:8".
